Name: Grassi Lakes
Description: Easy arrival-day hike right outside Canmore. Turquoise lakes beneath dramatic rock towers. 30-60 min from trailhead — perfect first taste of the Rockies.

Name: Policeman's Creek
Description: Flat evening walk through Canmore with Three Sisters peaks backdrop. Good sunset spot, central to town.

Name: Bow Valley Parkway
Description: Leave Canmore by 6am for the wildlife-rich dawn drive. Wolves, bears, and elk most active at first light on this 50 km alternative to Hwy 1. Drive slowly. Check seasonal closures before going.

Name: Johnston Canyon
Description: Best slot canyon hike in Banff — catwalk bolted into cliff face over rushing turquoise water. Lower Falls 2.7 km / Upper Falls 5.4 km return. Go early to beat crowds. Do not miss this.

Name: Banff townsite
Description: Use for supplies, lunch, and park info centre. Crowded in August — treat as a resupply stop rather than a destination. Pick up Parks Canada Discovery Pass here if not already done.

Name: Vermilion Lakes
Description: Best reflection photography in Banff. Beaver ponds with Mt. Rundle behind. Flat drive/walk just west of Banff townsite. Peak light is late afternoon — ideal on the way back from Johnston Canyon.

Name: Tunnel Mountain Summit
Description: Easy optional evening hike with aerial views over the whole Bow Valley. 4.8 km return, 300m gain. Good legs-stretch after a day of driving and walking.

Name: Lake Minnewanka
Description: Large cold mountain lake with dramatic front-range walls. Good for a paddle or lakeside walk if time allows.

Name: Cascade Ponds
Description: Low-effort lakeside stop under Cascade Mountain. Good for a picnic or decompression break near Banff.
